pr_title: copr: increase extra concurrency for small coprocessor tasks
pr_body:

PR Title Format:

### What problem does this PR solve?
<!--

Please create an issue first to describe the problem.

There MUST be one line starting with "Issue Number:  " and 
linking the relevant issues via the "close" or "ref".

For more info, check https://pingcap.github.io/tidb-dev-guide/contribute-to-tidb/contribute-code.html#referring-to-an-issue.

-->

Issue Number: close #37724

Problem Summary:

### What is changed and how it works?

When there are many small coprocessor tasks, the default value of `tidb_distsql_scan_concurrency` harms the latency. This PR increases extra concurrency when we exactly know there are small coprocessor tasks.

I tested this PR with the [script](https://gist.github.com/you06/3df2f6d00162cda4f4545728c5784c23).

Test result with different tidb_distsql_scan_concurrency before this PR

|tidb_distsql_scan_concurrency|latency|
|-|-|
|1|1.40s|
|2|647ms|
|4|299ms|
|8|141ms|
|16|67.0ms|
|32|41.0ms|
|64|34.4ms|
|128|33.9ms|
|256|32.2ms|

Tested with query shared into 1000 regions and got the following result(avg of 100 round test):

```
test with default tidb_distsql_scan_concurrency
before this PR: 70.2ms
after this PR:  33.2ms
```

issue_context.title: Optimize handle read in large cluster
issue_context.body:
## Enhancement

### Background

TiDB indexes data with global index, which lead to a problem that when data grows, some the required data may be sharded into many regions. One of those problem is when reading with indexlookup executor, the table scan may be divided into many coprocessor tasks.

![bad-indexlookup](https://user-images.githubusercontent.com/9587680/189129391-ac19d9d6-3e11-480e-b112-fffe724caaf0.png)

As the figure shows, the continuous index range may point to many discontinuous handle ranges in indexlookup executor. The default [`tidb_distsql_scan_concurrency`](https://github.com/pingcap/tidb/blob/e75a079d432ef0f40ae11b72ef61316d2e0adbd5/sessionctx/variable/tidb_vars.go#L839)  is 15, with a big number of handle read tasks, the concurrency is not sufficient and the latency increases. I wrote a [script](https://gist.github.com/you06/3df2f6d00162cda4f4545728c5784c23) to reproduce this issue.

### Solution

Note we can know the entries in handle ranges because TiDB guarantees the consistency of index and data, which means we already know the size of coprocessor tasks when reading handles, and we can adjust the concurrency by increasing the extra concurrency for small tasks. Small tasks won't block other queries on TiKV side because they are extremely fast(mostly less than 1ms on TiKV side).

review_comments: Better to add an example here as this part itself is quite complex and difficult to understand.

1. What happens if user set tidb_distsql_scan_concurrency bigger than 20?  Will it cause the SQL latency to be worse than before the feature was implemented?
2. If 20 is ok, why the default value 15 can not work well?

> Will it cause the SQL latency to be worse than before the feature was implemented?

The concurrency is adjusted in keep order mode, before the feature, concurrency will be reduced to 2 in this case and it's not affected by `tidb_distsql_scan_concurrency`, see [description](https://github.com/pingcap/tidb/blob/84fbfcada3d9564fe922771f010db318d27fc77a/store/copr/coprocessor.go#L149-L158).

> If 20 is ok, why the default value 15 can not work well?

This number is not carefully chosen, just set an upper limit.
Should we add a cross-region long range here?
